problem: MLLM-based embodied navigation agents see cluttered scenes where the key cues for the goal are overwhelmed by environmental noise, which leads to inefficient decisions.
motivation: Agents must focus on goal-relevant entities and regions to navigate robustly, but raw MLLM perception does not prioritize them. Scoring scene entities by semantic relevance to the goal could supply explicit language and visual guidance.
key_idea: Rank scene entities by semantic relevance to the navigation goal, add the top cues to the system prompt, and map them back into the image as explicit bounding boxes so the MLLM focuses on task-relevant content.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that combining structured language cues with visual bounding-box grounding helps suppress noise, but this is not verified here.
method: Semantic relevance evaluation: scores the correlation between scene entities and the navigation goal.
Ranked cue prompting: adds high-value ranked cues to the MLLM system prompt to guide language attention.
Visual grounding: maps the selected cues back into the visual space as explicit bounding boxes to guide visual attention.

setting.backbone: MLLM (specific model not stated in abstract)
